input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: After stripping ANSI codes the prompt text is also passed through str.strip(), which removes the whitespace at the end of the prompt that separates it from the user's typed input.
- failure path: click.prompt("Name") builds the prompt 'Name: '; when the stream does not support color (piped output, CliRunner, NO_COLOR) the prompt is shown as 'Name:' with the cursor glued to the colon, while on a color-capable terminal the same call keeps the trailing space, so transcripts differ between the two environments.

Reviewer finding
- description: When stripping applies, the prompt text is also whitespace-trimmed with .strip(), which the commit title does not mention. A prompt such as "Name: " is passed to input() as "Name:", dropping the separating space.
- rationale: Trigger: a prompt ending in a space (e.g. "Name: ") is read while the stream is not a TTY or color is disabled, so should_strip_ansi returns true. Mechanism: strip_ansi(text).strip() removes the trailing space, and the strip() also removes any leading whitespace. Impact: non-interactive or captured output shows "Name:" with no space, a visible change in prompt text beyond ANSI removal.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism as the label: `strip_ansi(text).strip()` removes the trailing space when ANSI stripping applies. It also gives the same trigger (non-TTY or color disabled) and the same effect, "Name: " becoming "Name:".
